newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung says Patten's home has bad fung shui.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung says Patten's home has bad fung shui.

text.p: Tung Chee-hwa, vying to lead Hong Kong after Britain withdraws next year, signalled on Thursday he was unlikely to move into the British Governor's official residence because of bad "fung shui".
"I have heard the Government House is crowded and the fung shui is not good," Tung told the China-controlled Selection Committee, which will choose Hong Kong's post-colonial leader.
Chinese rely on fung shui, or "wind and water", a system of harmonising people and their environment, to chart their lives -- their birthdays, weddings, business, even burials.
The 400-strong committee is vetting shipping tycoon Tung and two rivals at a three-day meeting before it picks the winner on December 11.
More than 150 years of colonial rule will end at midnight next June 30 and the Government House, the residence for all British Governors, will be vacated.
There has been talk of turning the colonial symbol into a museum. Tung said he supported the idea, but added the change would not be made immediately after the handover.
